 Cebu Mandaue probes private lot beside school 
 Mandaue City Mayor Thadeo Jovito “Jonkie” Ouano (Photo by ABC) April Blanche Cabañog Published on :  Nov 20, 2026, 5:48 am 
 Copied 
 RESIDENTS in Mandaue City have identified a private lot beside Opao Elementary School as a suspected mosquito breeding ground following reports of dengue infections and the deaths of two five-year-old kindergarten pupils in November 2026.
 Mayor Thadeo Jovito “Jonkie” Ouano said the City Government is trying to identify the property owner and secure permission to inspect the premises.
 Ouano visited Barangays Umapad and Opao on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, to assess the situation and meet local health officials.
 He said he learned that 15 other pupils from the same school had tested positive for dengue, raising concerns about a possible common source of mosquito exposure.
 “What could be their common denominator? They all attend the same school,” Ouano said.
 The mayor said the City tried to coordinate with two companies that residents believed owned the property.
 However, through the help of former Mandaue Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Mark Ynoc, officials learned that neither company owned the lot.
 The City has yet to establish ownership and gain access because security personnel guard the premises.
 Misting, cleanup 
 Ouano said officials need to inspect the property to determine whether it is indeed a mosquito breeding site before taking appropriate action.
 He emphasized that the City Government treats the dengue situation with urgency because of the deaths of young children.
 “Even if our dengue cases are lower, one life is already too many,” he said.
 After inspecting the barangays, Ouano met with City Health Office head Dr. Debra Maria Catulong at the Opao barangay hall to discuss measures to prevent further infections.
 The city continues to implement the 4S dengue prevention strategy, particularly “Seek and Destroy,” which encourages communities to identify and eliminate mosquito breeding sites.
 Ouano said the Department of Education (DepEd) had also requested another round of misting operations in all schools following the reported infections.
 The City will coordinate with the City Health Office to determine whether existing chemical supplies are sufficient or additional purchases are needed.
 He said previous cleanup and misting operations had been conducted in previous months, but the latest request from the DepEd prompted officials to consider another round to protect students.
 Prevention efforts 
 Ouano acknowledged parents’ fears, saying that as a parent himself, he understood their concerns.
 “I totally understand how they feel because I am also a parent,” he said, describing the deaths of the two children as heartbreaking.
 He also stressed the importance of early medical attention and monitoring, noting that dengue symptoms may initially appear mild even as a patient’s condition worsens.
 The City has designated dengue fast lanes in hospitals to accommodate suspected cases, he said, adding that medical interventions should follow the City Health Office’s recommendations.
 Ouano said the City would strengthen its prevention efforts and address residents’ concerns, expressing hope that no other family would suffer a similar loss. / ABC
